body.statement: Write \(\bar B_{nks}=N_{nks}^{-1}\sum_iB_{nksi}\) and \(\bar U^0_{nks}=N_{nks}^{-1}\sum_iU^0_{nksi}\). Under the empirical centered fourth-moment bound, the variance margin, and positive shares, eventually and uniformly over the finite set \((k,s)\in K\times S\), \[\frac{\max_i(B_{nksi}-\bar B_{nks})^2}{\sum_i(B_{nksi}-\bar B_{nks})^2}\le\frac{\sqrt{M_4N_{nks}}}{(N_{nks}-1)\epsilon}\longrightarrow0.\] Because \(0\le U^0_{nksi}\le1\), the normalized centered midranks satisfy \[\frac{\max_i(U^0_{nksi}-\bar U^0_{nks})^2}{\sum_i(U^0_{nksi}-\bar U^0_{nks})^2}\le\frac{1}{(N_{nks}-1)\epsilon}\longrightarrow0.\] Hence both finite-population maximum-influence conditions required by the joint permutation approximation are consequences of the primitive class conditions rather than separate assumptions.
body.justification: The finite-population Lindeberg ratios follow quantitatively from the maintained moment, variance, and positive-share primitives for every block in finite \(K\times S\).
body.gap: A maximum-influence premise would otherwise duplicate a condition already implied by observable finite-population bounds.
body.consumer: The vector randomization central limit theorem applies without an extra trial-population assumption.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a block and abbreviate its size by \(N\).  Since \(\max_i x_i^4\le\sum_i x_i^4\), the fourth-moment assumption implies
\[
\max_i(B_i-\bar B)^2
\le\left\{\sum_i(B_i-\bar B)^4\right\}^{1/2}
\le\sqrt{M_4N}.
\]
The variance margin gives \(\sum_i(B_i-\bar B)^2=(N-1)S_B^2\ge(N-1)\epsilon\).  Division proves the first displayed bound in the statement.  For normalized midranks, \(0\le U_i^0\le1\), so \(\max_i(U_i^0-\bar U^0)^2\le1\); the same variance-margin division proves the second bound.  Positive limiting shares imply \(N_{nks}\to\infty\) for every \((k,s)\), and, because \(K\times S\) is a fixed finite set, the convergence is uniform over all blocks.  Positivity of \(\epsilon\) justifies every division.
